messages.subject: Multiple Branches
parts:
Hello,

I want to define percentages for 3 branches, say 30%,20% and 50% respectively. What function should I use?

With this function they are sorted with the same percentage, that would be 33,3%

branch(function() sample(1:3, 1),continue=c(T,T,T),
         trajectory()%>%
           WH_(1),
         trajectory()%>%
           WH_(2),
         trajectory()%>%
           WH_(3)
         )

Regards,

The helper function works good, despite I didn't get exactly how it works. Now, could help me to code this if statement...

I want to do a separation of the arrivals (packages) by warehouse based on the attribute they receive from the dataframe. So there should be a step to check the value for the warehouse and then send the package to the respective trajectory. Now the code looks like this:

library(simmer)
set.seed(654)
env <- simmer()
workerCount <- 2

actualData <- data.frame(arrTime = c(1:10,1:5), 
                         warehouse = 1:3, 
                         duration = rnorm(15, 50, 5)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(arrTime)

consume <- function(x, prio=FALSE) {
  i <- 0
  function() {
    i <<- i + 1
    if (prio) c(x[[i]], x[[i]], FALSE)
    else x[[i]]
  }
}

AR1<-trajectory()%>%
  seize('worker') %>%
  timeout(function() get_attribute(env,"duration")) %>%
  release('worker')

AR2<-trajectory()%>%
  seize('worker') %>%
  timeout(function() get_attribute(env,"duration")) %>%
  release('worker')

activityTraj <- trajectory() %>%
  #set_prioritization(consume(actualData$priority, TRUE)) %>%
  set_attribute("duration", consume(actualData$duration)) %>%
  set_attribute("warehouse", consume(actualData$warehouse)) %>%
  join(function(){
    if (get_attribute(env,"warehouse")==1)  AR1
    else AR2
  })

env %>%
  add_resource('worker', workerCount, Inf, preemptive = TRUE) %>%
  add_generator('worker_', activityTraj, at(actualData$arrTime)) %>%
  run()
​

Thanks,

<victor.hu...@gmail.com>:

> The helper function works good, despite I didn't get exactly how it works.
> Now, could help me to code this if statement...

Given that you don't need to assign priorities, just attributes, the
helper function can be simplified as follows:

consume <- function(x) {

i <- 0
function() {
i <<- i + 1

x[[i]]
}
}

This helper returns a closure. Each call increments the index and
returns the corresponding element from the x vector. That's how it
works.

> I want to do a separation of the arrivals (packages) by warehouse based on
> the attribute they receive from the dataframe. So there should be a step to
> check the value for the warehouse and then send the package to the
> respective trajectory.

The join() method does not accept a function as input. You need a branch():

branch(
get_attribute(env,"warehouse")==1,
continue=c(TRUE, TRUE),
AR1, AR2
)

>
> library(simmer)
> set.seed(654)
> env <- simmer()
> workerCount <- 2
>
> actualData <- data.frame(arrTime = c(1:10,1:5),
> warehouse = 1:3,
> duration = rnorm(15, 50, 5)) %>%
> dplyr::arrange(arrTime)
>
> consume <- function(x, prio=FALSE) {
> i <- 0
> function() {
> i <<- i + 1
> if (prio) c(x[[i]], x[[i]], FALSE)
> else x[[i]]
> }
> }
>
> AR1<-trajectory()%>%
> seize('worker') %>%
> timeout(function() get_attribute(env,"duration")) %>%
> release('worker')
>
> AR2<-trajectory()%>%
> seize('worker') %>%
> timeout(function() get_attribute(env,"duration")) %>%
> release('worker')
>
> activityTraj <- trajectory() %>%
> #set_prioritization(consume(actualData$priority, TRUE)) %>%
> set_attribute("duration", consume(actualData$duration)) %>%
> set_attribute("warehouse", consume(actualData$warehouse)) %>%
> join(function(){
> if (get_attribute(env,"warehouse")==1) AR1
> else AR2
> })
>
> env %>%
> add_resource('worker', workerCount, Inf, preemptive = TRUE) %>%
> add_generator('worker_', activityTraj, at(actualData$arrTime)) %>%
> run()
>
>
